title: SE-keyed anti-phishing words at PIN entry (Coldcard / Passport 'Security Words'): detect a swapped or cloned device before the full PIN is typed
threat: Evil-maid / reseller swap: a look-alike device (or an implanted one with its own firmware) harvests the PIN as the user types it on the trusted UI; the boot fingerprint proves the firmware, not that this is the user's own unit, and a device with the same firmware shows the same 8 words.
proposal: After the first 4 PIN digits, compute inside an SE (SE050 HMAC over the prefix with a per-device SE-resident secret, or OPTIGA CMAC via a protected object, rate-limited by SE policy to ~2 s per distinct prefix) and render two BIP-39 words via the CT secret path; the user learns them at setup (shown once, written next to the device) and aborts PIN entry if they differ. Opt-in (Passport default-off) or default-on with an explicit setup step. Keep PIN comparison itself in SE silicon (invariant #2 untouched; the prefix MAC is a separate keyed object, never the PIN object).
rationale: Zero hardware cost, directly addresses the user's 'malicious hardware' question for the swap case (a clone cannot reproduce the SE-keyed words), and complements the FSBL fingerprint which only answers 'which firmware'.
repo_evidence: secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs:8-30 (F-20 only; no device-authenticity words); grep anti-phish/security words/prefix in pin_entry.rs, cmd_request_unlock.rs, threat-model.md, trezor-comparison.md: none
secure/src/ui/secret_text.rs:73-82 (CT secret row primitive available to render the words)
vendor_precedent: Coldcard Mk4 anti-phishing words (HMAC over hashed PIN prefix in SE1, 2 s rate limit); Foundation Passport Prime 'Security Words' (off by default).
risks: Exposes a rate-limited 4-digit-prefix oracle on the SE (10,000 prefixes; with 2 s/attempt ~5.5 h to enumerate, which reveals the PIN prefix only if the user's words are known — the words are secret to the user, so the oracle yields nothing to an attacker without them). The words themselves become a secret displayed every unlock — must go through the CT/forced path (D-01) and the constant-weight pair (D-04). Needs an SE050 object/policy design and an attempt-counter interaction review so it cannot consume page-124/E120 budget.
